info.title: Coco API
info.description:
Contract v2, served under `/api/v2`: the v1 API in English and camelCase, with every
list paginated as `{ data, meta: { page, perPage, total } }`.

Every successful JSON response is wrapped as `{ data, meta }`. Every error is
`application/problem+json` (RFC 9457): `{ type, title, status, detail, code, errors? }`.
Switch on `code`: stable, in English, one per business rule. `errors` lists the fields
that failed.
Messages meant for the user are in Spanish.

Identifiers are integers (int64) and money travels as a decimal string.

field.description: Path of the field at fault (`splits.0.amount`), when there is one.

message.description: In Spanish: the client may show it next to the field.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable: one per business rule (`problem-codes.ts`).

title.description: Short summary of the kind of problem, in Spanish; the same for every occurrence.

detail.description: What happened this time, in Spanish: the client may show it as is.

errors.description: One per invalid field; present only when the input itself is at fault.

pendingApproval.description: Whether an administrator must approve the account before it can sign in.

message.description: In Spanish: the client shows it as is.

refreshToken.description: Native clients only (`X-Coco-Client: native`); the web gets an httpOnly cookie instead.

parentId.description: `null` for a cost center, the top of the tree.

isRecurring.description: Whether the concept is paid every so often.

isStatic.description: Whether the cost center refuses reclassification from the transactions table.

paymentDay.description: Day of the month it is due.

paymentMonth.description: Reference month of the cycle, 1–12. Only when the periodicity is not monthly.

budget.description: Expected cost each time, as a decimal string.

isAutoPaid.description: Whether the transaction is created on its own on the due day.

isMultiPayment.description: Whether it is paid in several parts rather than settled at once.

keywords.description: Words looked for in a receipt to recognise this concept.
